set_text.text: What is an early payment discount?

An early payment discount is a price cut your supplier offers if you pay an invoice before the due date. It is written as terms such as 2/10 net 30: 2% off within 10 days, or the full amount by day 30. In effect, the supplier pays you to settle 20 days sooner.
An offer, not a term you owe
Skip it and you simply pay $22.56 a case by day 30. Take it and the same case is $22.11, paid by day 10.
Day 11 is too late. Taking the 2% after the window is called an unearned discount, and suppliers often bill it back.
Offering it costs the same rate
If you offer 2/10 net 30 to your own accounts, the math runs the other way. An account that would otherwise pay on day 30 costs you 37.2% a year to pay 20 days sooner.
Who uses an early payment discount calculator
It is for independent food distributors who buy from suppliers on terms. Whoever approves supplier invoices, plans the payment run or negotiates terms should run it first.
